paragraphs.text: Here we present formulas that facilitate the practical computation of {{E}^{\textup{FSW}}} , and then analyze its computational complexity.
We start by introducing notation that shall be used to express quantile functions of distributions in {\mathcal{P}_{\leq N}(\mathbb{R})} .

We now show how {{Q}}_{\mu}(t) can be expressed explicitly in terms of the order statistics of the support of \mu . Let \mu=\sum_{i=1}^{N}w_{i}x_{i}\in{\mathcal{P}_{\leq N}(\mathbb{R})} and denote {{\bm{x}}}={\left({x_{1},\ldots,x_{N}}\right)} , {{\bm{w}}}={\left({w_{1},\ldots,w_{N}}\right)} . Then for all t\in\left[0,1\right) , it can be shown that {{Q}}_{\mu}(t)=x_{{\left({{k_{\min}(\sigma({{\bm{x}}}),{{\bm{w}}},t)}}\right)}}, (20) where k_{\min}(\sigma,{{\bm{w}}},t) is defined for \sigma={\left({\sigma_{1},\ldots,\sigma_{N}}\right)}\in S_{N} by k_{\min}(\sigma,{{\bm{w}}},t)\coloneqq\min{\left\{{k\in{\left[{N}\right]}}{\ \,}\middle|{\ \,}{w_{\sigma_{1}}+\cdots+w_{\sigma_{k}}>t}\right\}}. (21) It can be seen in 20 and 21 that {{Q}}_{\mu}(t) is monotone increasing with respect to t . Moreover, {{Q}}_{\mu}(0)=\textup{ess}\min(\mu)\quad\text{and}\quad\lim_{t\nearrow 1}{{Q}}_{\mu}(t)=\textup{ess}\max(\mu), with \textup{ess}\min(\mu) and \textup{ess}\max(\mu) denoting the essential minimum and maximum of the distribution \mu . We thus augment the definition of {{Q}}_{\mu} to {\left[{0,1}\right]} by setting {{Q}}_{\mu}(1)=\textup{ess}\max(\mu) .

Using the identity 20 , {{E}}(\mu;{{\bm{v}}},\xi) can be expressed as \begin{split}{{E}}(\mu;{{\bm{v}}},\xi)=&2{\left({1+\xi}\right)}\sum_{k=1}^{N}\int_{t=\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}w_{{\sigma_{i}({{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X})}}}^{\sum_{i=1}^{k}w_{{\sigma_{i}({{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X})}}}{{Q}}_{{{\bm{v}}}^{T}\mu}(t)\cos(2\pi\xi t)dt\\ =&2{\left({1+\xi}\right)}\sum_{k=1}^{N}\int_{t=\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}w_{{\sigma_{i}({{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X})}}}^{\sum_{i=1}^{k}w_{{\sigma_{i}({{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X})}}}{\left({{{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X}}\right)}_{{\left({{k}}\right)}}\cos(2\pi\xi t)dt\\ =&2\frac{1+\xi}{2\pi\xi}\sum_{k=1}^{N}{\left({{{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X}}\right)}_{{\left({{k}}\right)}}{\left[{\sin(2\pi\xi t)}\right]}_{t=\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}w_{{\sigma_{i}({{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X})}}}^{\sum_{i=1}^{k}w_{{\sigma_{i}({{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X})}}},\end{split} (22) under the notion \sum_{i=1}^{0}w_{{\sigma_{i}({{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X})}}=0 . Rearranging terms gives us the alternative formula \begin{split}{{E}}(\mu;{{\bm{v}}},\xi)=2\frac{1+\xi}{2\pi\xi}\sum_{k=1}^{N}\sin(2\pi\xi{\sum_{i=1}^{k}w_{{\sigma_{i}({{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X})}}}){\left[{{\left({{{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X}}\right)}_{{\left({{k}}\right)}}-{\left({{{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X}}\right)}_{{\left({{k+1}}\right)}}}\right]},\end{split} (23) with the definition of {\left({{{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X}}\right)}_{{\left({{k}}\right)}} extended to k=N+1 by {\left({{{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X}}\right)}_{{\left({{N+1}}\right)}}\coloneqq 0. To prevent numerical instability for values of \xi near zero, the explicit division by 2\pi\xi can be avoided by replacing the sine function in 23 with the normalized sinc function {\textup{sinc}}(x)\coloneqq\begin{cases}\frac{\sin(\pi x)}{\pi x},&x\neq 0,\\ 0,&x=0,\end{cases} which is implemented in a numerically stable way in most standard numerical libraries.

This yields the alternative formulas to 22 and 23 : \begin{split}{{E}}(\mu;{{\bm{v}}},\xi)=2{\left({1+\xi}\right)}\sum_{k=1}^{N}{\left({{{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X}}\right)}_{{\left({{k}}\right)}}{\left[{t\cdot{{\textup{sinc}}(2\xi t)}}\right]}_{t=\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}w_{{\sigma_{i}({{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X})}}}^{\sum_{i=1}^{k}w_{{\sigma_{i}({{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X})}}},\end{split} (24) and \begin{split}{{E}}(\mu;{{\bm{v}}},\xi)=2{\left({1+\xi}\right)}\sum_{k=1}^{N}{\left({{\sum_{i=1}^{k}w_{{\sigma_{i}({{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X})}}}}\right)}{{\textup{sinc}}(2\xi{\sum_{i=1}^{k}w_{{\sigma_{i}({{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X})}}})}{\left[{{\left({{{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X}}\right)}_{{\left({{k}}\right)}}-{\left({{{\bm{v}}}^{T}\bm{X}}\right)}_{{\left({{k+1}}\right)}}}\right]}.\end{split} (25)
